question: The process of forming a thick layer of aluminium oxide on the surface of aluminium so as to protect it from corrosion is called:
solution:
The correct answer is **Anodising.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__​**

__
 
• The process of** anodizing involves employing aluminium **as an anode in an electrolyte bath.
 
• when a** cathode is placed inside the anodizing tank** and the medium is delivered a current through it.
 
• The** electrochemical process of anodizing transforms the metal surface **into an attractive, long-lasting, corrosion-resistant anodic oxide finish.
 
• The** anode is created using the components **and a weak acid solution. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__​​​​​​​**

 
• **Roasting is a method of slow cooking** that uses diffused, indirect heat to roast its contents.
 
• Applying a protective zinc coating to steel or iron to stop rusting is the **process of galvanization.**
 
• Calcination is the term for applying heat to a **solid chemical substance. **
